title: Paediatric Dehydration and Acute Gastroenteritis: Assessment and Rehydration Pathway

evidenceAudit.scope: Paediatric Dehydration and Acute Gastroenteritis: Assessment and Rehydration Pathway
findings: Built as an additive Disease Management version using the approved-topic structure.
Investigations are ordered from bedside/laboratory assessment to imaging and specialist tests.
The original outline remains current; this version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: Saudi paediatric IV-fluid and ORS product policy was not opened.
This topic is scoped to under-5s because CG84 is the opened source.

pathophysiology.summary: Vomiting and diarrhoea cause water and electrolyte loss. Reduced circulating volume progresses from clinical dehydration to shock. Low-osmolarity oral rehydration replaces water and electrolytes through intestinal cotransport.
keyMechanisms: Vomiting and diarrhoea cause water and electrolyte loss.
Reduced circulating volume progresses from clinical dehydration to shock.
Low-osmolarity oral rehydration replaces water and electrolytes through intestinal cotransport.

symptoms: Diarrhoea, vomiting, reduced intake, thirst or reduced urine output.
physicalSigns: General appearance, responsiveness, eyes, mucosa, heart rate, breathing, pulses, capillary refill and skin turgor determine severity.
redFlags: Shock, altered responsiveness, weak pulses, prolonged capillary refill, tachypnoea, bilious vomiting, blood/mucus in stool or severe localised abdominal pain.
precipitants: Viral gastroenteritis, bacterial infection, inadequate replacement or high-risk comorbidity.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Bilious vomiting, peritonism or focal severe pain.
Systemic toxicity or shock disproportionate to gastrointestinal loss.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Select oral versus intravenous pathway and reassess frequently.
ruleIn.normalValue: Normal responsiveness, pulses, mucosa and urine output

ruleIn.testName: Blood glucose in altered or high-risk child
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Treat immediately and investigate an alternative/complicating diagnosis.

ruleIn.testName: Electrolytes, urea and creatinine when IV fluids are required
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Sodium disturbance, renal impairment or acidosis
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Guide IV fluid composition and monitoring; not routine in uncomplicated oral rehydration.
Use for blood/mucus, immunocompromise, prolonged illness, travel or outbreak/public-health indication.

ruleOut.expectedFinding: Ongoing loss or failure to rehydrate
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Document intake, losses, urine and serial weight when admitted.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess and exclude shock
actions: Use the NICE dehydration/shock table and assess for red flags or alternative diagnosis.
In shock, obtain senior help and start the intravenous pathway immediately.

clinicalManagement.title: Rehydrate
actions: For clinical dehydration without shock, give low-osmolarity ORS 50 mL/kg over 4 hours plus maintenance, frequently in small amounts.
Continue breastfeeding and replace ongoing large watery stools with ORS according to the source pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Reassess and discharge safely
actions: Reassess hydration and oral tolerance; escalate persistent vomiting or deterioration.
Give return precautions and feeding/hygiene advice.

regimens.patientGroup: Child under 5 with clinical dehydration without shock
regimens.dose: 50 mL/kg over 4 hours in addition to maintenance; give frequently in small amounts
regimens.frequency: Continuous small frequent amounts over 4 hours
regimens.duration: Reassess after 4 hours; continue replacement for ongoing losses as directed
adjustments: Use the shock/IV pathway when shock is present.
Seek specialist advice for electrolyte disorder, renal/cardiac disease or severe malnutrition.
Check Saudi hospital product and protocol.
monitoring: Clinical hydration, vomiting, stool losses, urine output and weight when indicated.
contraindications: Shock, ileus or inability to protect the airway for oral administration.

branches.label: Clinical dehydration without shock
branches.entryCriteria: Under-5 child with clinical dehydration and no shock.

medicationPlan.note: Oral rehydration is preferred when there is no shock; IV boluses and maintenance must follow the local paediatric fluid policy.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Use the NICE CG84 symptom/sign table; shock features override routine oral rehydration.

teaching.scope: Paediatric Dehydration and Acute Gastroenteritis: Assessment and Rehydration Pathway
learningObjectives: Recognise the emergency and relevant red flags.
Select the correct investigation and escalation pathway.
Use medicines only within the stated branch and local formulary.
pitfalls: Delaying specialist escalation while waiting for a non-essential test.
Using an unverified medicine dose or applying an adult pathway to a child.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval.
keyPoints: Shock, altered responsiveness, weak pulses, prolonged capillary refill, tachypnoea, bilious vomiting, blood/mucus in stool or severe localised abdominal pain.

patientEducation: Teach ORS preparation/use, continued feeding and red-flag return precautions.
lifestyleAndDiet: Continue breastfeeding and usual milk feeds after rehydration; avoid fruit juice and carbonated drinks until diarrhoea stops.
mdtReferrals: Paediatrics for shock, high-risk comorbidity, diagnostic uncertainty or failed oral rehydration.
dischargeCriteria: No shock, hydration improved, oral intake tolerated and caregivers can continue fluids with safety-net advice.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Primary-care/paediatric review if symptoms persist or red flags develop.
